chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever associates, alongside an Imam whose Imamate is from Allah, one whose Imamate is not from Allah, has committed shirk with Allah.

key_terms.أَشْرَكَ: associated a partner; ascribed partnership in a matter belonging solely to Allah
key_terms.إِمَامَتُهُ: his Imamate; his rightful authority and leadership
key_terms.مُشْرِكًا بِاللَّهِ: one committing shirk with Allah; one guilty of associating partners with Allah
key_terms.مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ: from the Presence of Allah; divinely appointed by Allah

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about recognizing an Imam not appointed by Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms that true Imamate is only that which is appointed by Allah. To place alongside a divinely appointed Imam someone whose Imamate is not from Allah is described as shirk, underscoring the gravity of religious authority and legitimacy in creed.
